text: In the NARMA-10 spectral-radius sweep, why is the test-NMSE curve U-shaped in rho?
choices: NMSE is minimized at rho = 0 and increases monotonically with rho
Small rho gives too little memory for the 10-step dependency, while rho > 1 loses the ESP so the dynamics diverge
Small rho diverges immediately while large rho always generalizes best
The curve is U-shaped only because the code caps NMSE at 10
explanation: NARMA-10 depends on the past ~10 inputs. When rho is too small (< 0.5) the reservoir's memory horizon is far shorter than 10 steps, so error is high; when rho > 1 the ESP is lost and trajectories diverge, so error is high again. The minimum sits near rho ~ 0.8-0.95. rho = 0 has essentially no memory (not the optimum), large rho does NOT generalize best, and the NMSE cap only prevents diverged values from dominating the plot, it does not create the U-shape.
